messages.subject: Calibration question
parts:
Dear Adrian,

I have a question about working with fsqca that may seem pretty trivial, nevertheless it is still bothersome.

When choosing to calibrate manually, I wonder if the range could be approached holistically or if the process of calibration is strictly bound to the data at hand:

Let's say we want to measure something like modernity in a data-set that only contains countries from the EU. Is it possible for me to start my calibration at 0.5 with the underlying logic that there are other countries outside the EU that, were they in this data-set, would be the ones  considered more out than in the set?

Would I be artificially inflating the size of some sets given the fact that some of my other variables have go below 0.5? Would this logic create problems when doing the necessity and sufficiency analysis?


Multumesc frumos :)
Valentina Moraru

messages.author: a98c47479ea6b61f
messages.subject: Re: [QCA] Calibration question
parts:
Dear Valentina,

Theoretically, it is possible for you to do anything :)
Whether it will produce the intended results, that is a different question...

First and foremost, I would not advise manual calibration because that is so very subjective. Different researchers might reach different conclusions just because of subjectively choosing different fuzzy scores. You can do that of course, and there are many papers using this (so-called) "direct assignment", but my methodological choice follows a more principial direct or indirect method, using numeric raw data to obtain the set membership scores.

Second and perhaps most important, calibrating all scores above 0.5 is pointless because it would make that variable a constant (all values equal to 1) in the truth table. The whole point of the QCA is to compare among the observed cases (despite they are a subset of a larger population). QCA, just like regular statistics, needs variation to differentiate between "positive" cases and "negative" cases.

While your proposal would only produce constant "positive" cases in the truth table procedure, hence not very useful in the overall solution, either for sufficiency and for necessity.

In hoping this is helpful (cu multa placere),
Adrian
